name: Discontinuous Displacement Mapping for Volume Graphics
definition: A volume rendering technique that displaces a proxy scene geometry (bounding box) using a displacement texture to sample an original object texture, handling discontinuities via an alpha mask to avoid interpolation artifacts.
summary: Discontinuous Displacement Mapping is a volume rendering technique that deforms proxy geometry using 3D textures to handle cuts and fractures via alpha masks, preventing interpolation artifacts and maintaining correct lighting at boundaries.
